title: Several things look wrong in a race recording (agateau/pixelwheels #362, temporal_interaction)
eyebrow: QC review · task109 Attempt5 (re-check after the dim 11 fix)
verdict_reason: One dimension fails: Instruction – Symptom Specificity (dim 4, [Fail - Unspecific Symptoms]). The instruction names three elements (what a vehicle carries, shadows, the race view). The fired rocket's flight direction and its flame are covered by none of them: a fired rocket is no longer carried, no phrase names a flame or exhaust, and the only remaining cover is the stand-alone 'several things ... don't look the way they normally do' / 'Which things ... can be seen in the recording'. The carried rocket's orientation is implied only weakly, and the single example given ('show through something that covers the vehicle') steers readers to draw order: 3 of 4 with-image runs treated it as the whole carried-item defect. The other 18 dimensions score 5. The Attempt4 failure, Tests – Implementation Overfit (dim 11), is fixed: golden + the Mine-style tint of the carried rocket now scores 1.0 (0.0 with 3 NullPointerExceptions under the Attempt4 tests), and Attempt4's jmtBZi2 submission now loses only its genuine exhaust miss (6/7 instead of 3/7). Difficulty holds: 0/3 no-image and exactly 1/4 with-image (2uvoT9Z). CB Oracle 1.0, CB Nop 0.0, local oracle 1.0 twice, local nop 0.0; Check and Analyze pass everything.

dimensions.name: Instruction – Requires Visual Evidence
dimensions.evidence: Read without the video, instruction.md now states three symptoms in words: something a vehicle carries 'can show through something that covers the vehicle, instead of being hidden with it'; some shadows 'don't fall or turn like the others in the clip'; and the race view 'sometimes shows more of the road behind the vehicle it follows than ahead of it'. Beyond that it only says that some of what a vehicle carries is 'drawn or hidden wrongly compared with that vehicle'. It names no object, timestamp, file, repo or mechanism. The no-image trials show the text is still not enough for a complete fix. In every no-image run /app/.harbor_assets was empty ('total 8', only . and ..), and each scored f2p 4/7. All three fixed the z-order, both shadows and the camera from the text plus a code audit. All three failed carriedRocketPointsWhereTheCarPoints, firedRocketFliesWhereTheCarPoints and rocketExhaustComesOutOfItsTail with exactly the nop values (rocket drawn at 278.8665°, flew towards 278.87335°, exhaust at -0.34987 along the axis), so the rocket's orientation and flame (bugs 01-03) still need the video. The path resolves: the Dockerfile has `COPY assets/recording.mp4 /app/.harbor_assets/`. Leak check: instruction.md names no repo, URL, file list, object or mechanism. The mechanism and timestamps appear only in task.toml, which is blind (task_manifest.json blind list: tests/, solution/, task.toml).
dimensions.wrong: Nothing found. Non-graded: the camera symptom is now stated in text too, so 4 of the 7 f2p (z-order, both shadows, camera) can be fixed without the video, the same 4 as in Attempt4. V27 only needs the text to fall short of a complete fix, and it does: 3 f2p (2 of the 6 defects) still need the video.

dimensions.name: Instruction – Symptom Specificity
dimensions.evidence:
WHAT CHANGED vs Attempt4: '(it can show through something that covers the vehicle)' became '(it can show through something that covers the vehicle, instead of being hidden with it)', and 'the race view doesn't follow the action the way it should' became 'the race view sometimes shows more of the road behind the vehicle it follows than ahead of it'. The shadow sentence is unchanged.
TABLE (element | defect: text or image? | expected: text or image? | comparison pointed to | clue left to image | described correctly?)
1. 'what a vehicle carries' (the rocket on the car, its flight and its flame) | z-order: TEXT, 'it can show through something that covers the vehicle'. Orientation (crosswise on the car at 0-1.2 s and under the bridge at 9.2-9.5 s; fired sideways into the fence at 9.85-10.05 s) and flame (out of the rocket's side at 9.87-9.97 s): kind only, 'drawn ... wrongly compared with that vehicle'; the exact defect is in the IMAGE | z-order: TEXT, 'instead of being hidden with it'. Orientation and flame: IMAGE, via 'the same kind of thing is drawn correctly elsewhere in the same clip' (the car's own boost flame comes out of its back at 6.6-7.0 s) | in-clip comparison | which object (rocket), what covers it (footbridge), when, how far off | z-order and carried orientation: yes, checked on sheet_2 (countdown), sheet_4b (footbridge), sheet_5 and the new close-up sheet_6 (launch). The carried orientation is only weakly implied: the single example given is the draw-order one.
1b. the FIRED rocket's flight direction (sideways into the fence, 9.85-10.05 s) | MISSING: a fired rocket is no longer 'what a vehicle carries', and no other phrase names it | MISSING | only the stand-alone 'the same kind of thing is drawn correctly elsewhere' | everything | element not named by type.
1c. the rocket's FLAME (out of its side, 9.87-9.97 s) | MISSING: no phrase names a flame or exhaust | MISSING (the car's own boost flame at 6.6-7.0 s is the in-clip reference, but the text never points at flames) | only 'several things ... don't look the way they normally do' / 'Which things ... can be seen in the recording', which stand alone | everything | element not named by type.
2. 'some shadows' | TEXT: 'don't fall or turn like the others' | TEXT + IMAGE: like the others in the clip | in-clip comparison | which shadows (car shadow up-left in the countdown; rocket and crate shadows that don't turn) | yes.
3. 'the race view' | TEXT: 'sometimes shows more of the road behind the vehicle it follows than ahead of it' | TEXT: by implication, more of the road ahead | not needed | which stretches (the east/west straights; at 8 s the car is at the left edge heading west) | yes. This upgrades the Attempt4 wording, which named only the kind of problem.
THE THREE CHECKS: (1) an element is named for all three areas, with no fix hint. (2) every general phrase comes with its context right away (compared with that vehicle / like the others / behind vs ahead), plus the in-clip pointer. (3) the clues (which instance, when, how big) stay in the clip. The z-order, both shadows and the camera are now stated in text, and the carried orientation is at least covered by kind ('drawn ... wrongly compared with that vehicle'). Check (1) fails for rows 1b and 1c: the fired rocket's flight and its flame are never named by type, so the only text covering them is a generic phrase standing alone. That is the [Fail - Unspecific Symptoms] pattern ('doesn't name the element by type'), not the image-carried 3, which needs the element named.
TRAJECTORIES (all 4 with-image runs read in full): every run named the rocket drawn over the footbridge as a bug and fixed it, and all 4 fixed both shadow defects and the camera. 2uvoT9Z reported that the carried missile 'showed over the bridge and pointed the wrong way (around 9-10 s, when the car drives under the bridge)', fixed the creation angle ('Pointing across the car') and also fixed the exhaust axis, which it called a 'Related fix, not visible in the clip'. 4rZRzDa, atD2psm and bmqmxkm never mention the rocket's orientation, its flight direction or its flame: they treated the 'show through' example as the whole carried-item defect, and atD2psm and bmqmxkm extended the z-order fix to carried mines. A grep of all 4 runs for 'intended', 'by design', 'looks fine/right/correct', 'not a bug' and 'left ... alone' finds no defect described as intended. The Analyze job agrees: task_specification = pass for all 4, with the misses put down to frame sampling that never looked closely at the launch (each failing run stopped after about 2 minutes of its 90-minute budget).
'NOT VISIBLE IN THE CLIP' CHECKED: the flame defect is visible. In sheet_6 (2x zoom of 9.80-9.97 s) the fired rocket heads down toward the fence with its flame beside its body, not behind its tail, from 9.87 s on. 2uvoT9Z's close-up crops (steps 8-11, 8.5-10.1 s) all framed the area around the footbridge (y 150-650 of 1080), above the rocket's flight path (y about 600-900), and its only frames of the launch are 2-fps overviews at half resolution or less. The remark is a sampling miss, not a gap in the asset.
dimensions.wrong: Two of the six defects have no element named in the text. The fired rocket's flight direction is not 'what a vehicle carries', and nothing names a flame or exhaust, so rocketExhaustComesOutOfItsTail (and the fired half of the angle defect) rests only on the stand-alone 'several things ... don't look the way they normally do'. The carried orientation is implied only by kind, and the one example given ('show through something that covers the vehicle') steers readers to draw order. The trials show that narrowing: 3 of the 4 with-image runs (4rZRzDa, atD2psm, bmqmxkm) treated the 'show through' example as the whole carried-item defect and never looked at the rocket's orientation, flight or flame. None called a defect intended, so the fail rests on the missing elements, not on the 'agents couldn't tell' clause.
dimensions.fix: Name the missing elements by type and point to the comparison, without stating what correct looks like (stating it, as Attempt1 did with 'face the same way' / 'trails out behind it', let all 3 no-image runs pass). Suggested line: 'Some of what a vehicle carries or fires is drawn wrongly compared with that vehicle: it can show through something that covers the vehicle instead of being hidden with it, and how it is turned, where it goes once fired and where its flame comes out don't match the same kind of thing elsewhere in the clip.' That reaches the image-carried 3. It also tells a no-image solver to audit the rocket's angle and flame code, so the no-image pass risk goes up. Changing instruction.md changes the checksum: re-run Oracle, Nop and all trials (Option B, 3 no-image + 8 with-image with 1-2 passes, tolerates the spread better).

dimensions.name: Instruction – Task Type
dimensions.evidence: task_type = temporal_interaction: 'Fix a defect that only appears across a sequence of interactions / state transitions'. The defects show up across transitions in the clip. The rocket shows over the footbridge only while the car passes under it (9.25-9.33 s). The fired rocket's path and flame appear only after launch (9.85-10.05 s). The look-ahead error depends on the heading as the lap goes on (east/west vs north/south stretches). The Attempt5 wording (a carried thing showing through a cover instead of being hidden with the vehicle, shadows that don't fall or turn like the others, a view that sometimes shows more road behind than ahead) describes drawing and view problems over the course of a recorded race, which fits the type.
dimensions.wrong: Nothing found. Two of the six defects (the crosswise rocket and the car shadow) are visible in a single frame. That is fine, since the task as a whole needs the sequence.

NAMING TABLE (file | role | what the frames show | what name/role/text claim | true? | agents confused?): recording.mp4 | bug_video | base behavior with bugs 01-05 injected. 0-1.2 s countdown: rocket crosswise on a north-facing car, car shadow up-left (sheet_2). 9.18-9.40 s: car hidden under the footbridge while the rocket and a flat rocket shadow are drawn over it (sheet_4b). 9.80-10.2 s: rocket fired, heading down into the fence while the car heads west, flame beside the rocket's body from 9.87 s (sheet_6), explosion at the fence at about 10.05 s (sheet_5). 6.6-7.0 s: the car's own boost flame comes out of its back (sheet_3). 8 s: car at the left edge heading west (sheet_1) | neutral name; role 'bug_video'; the ASSET_MANIFEST and evidence_bundle descriptions (countdown, lap, footbridge, launch, explosion at the fence) | true | no: no run treated the video as a reference, all 4 with-image runs read the footbridge frames as the bug, and 2uvoT9Z read the wrongly pointing rocket correctly. 2uvoT9Z's claim that the flame defect is 'not visible in the clip' was checked and is wrong (sheet_6; see dim 4). dimensions.name: Tests – Implementation Overfit
dimensions.evidence:
WHAT CHANGED: test.patch now stubs the renderer on both mocked racers with `when(racer.getVehicleRenderer()).thenReturn(new VehicleRenderer(assets, vehicle));`, under the comment 'A real Racer always has a VehicleRenderer; code drawing what it carries may use it.' In RocketTest it follows the turboFlame field set-up (plus the VehicleRenderer import); in MissileZOrderTest it comes just before `return Missile.create(...)`. This is what the game does (Racer.java:127: `mVehicleRenderer = new VehicleRenderer(assets, mVehicle)`), and the VehicleRenderer and SkidmarksRenderer constructors don't touch GL. The two hunk headers (+1,282 and +1,397) and the index lines were regenerated, and test.patch applies cleanly in every CB and local run ('== applying test.patch ==', no 'could not apply'). No assertion changed.
EQUIVALENCE TABLE (alternative | correct & in repo context? | test accepts? | evidence):
(A) golden ZLevel split (FLYING_LOW / FG_LAYERS / FLYING_HIGH) | yes | yes | CB Oracle Hk5pFie and local oracle x2: 7/7, 2/2.
(B) carried missile drawn at its vehicle's ZLevel, fired missile on top | yes, plausible | yes | all 4 with-image runs (2uvoT9Z, 4rZRzDa, atD2psm, bmqmxkm) pass missileIsDrawnBeforeForegroundLayer with it.
(C) golden + tint the carried missile with its vehicle's batch colour, unconditionally, as Mine.draw does (the Attempt4 failure) | yes | YES (was NO) | local alt_tint: 1.0, 7/7, 2/2, no NullPointerException; under the Attempt4 tests the same code scored 0.0 (4/7, 3 NPEs). TRIAL EVIDENCE: Attempt4's jmtBZi2 wrote this tint. Its submission replayed on the Attempt5 tests gives 6/7 and fails only rocketExhaustComesOutOfItsTail ('the exhaust should be behind the rocket's tail, it is -0.35 along the rocket axis'), a genuine miss. Under the Attempt4 tests it lost 3 more f2p to the NPE (3/7).
(C2) tint only while the car is falling (2uvoT9Z: `if (vehicle.isFalling()) batch.setColor(mShooter.getVehicleRenderer().getBatchColor());`) | yes | yes | 2uvoT9Z 1.0 on the CB; local replay 1.0 on the Attempt5 tests and also 1.0 on the Attempt4 tests, because no test makes the car fall, so this branch never asks for the renderer. Its pass therefore does not exercise the new stub; (C) and the jmtBZi2 replay do.
(D) rocket angle: golden degRad / vehicle.getBody().getAngle() / referenceAngle = 0 | yes | yes | 2uvoT9Z used normalizeAnglePiRad(vehicle.getBody().getAngle()) and passed both rocket-angle f2p.
(E) exhaust by cos/sin (golden) or set(refH, 0).rotateRad | yes, same vector | yes | 2uvoT9Z (mReactorPos.set(refH, 0)).
(F) shadow angle radDeg in BodyRegionDrawer | yes | yes | all 7 trials pass rocketShadowHasTheRocketsOrientation.
(G) car shadow sign flip | yes | yes | all 7 trials pass vehicleShadowFallsLikeEveryOtherShadow.
(H) look-ahead built along the heading, with or without moving the camera speed clamp | yes, same vector | yes | all 7 trials pass viewLooksAheadOfTheCarWhicheverWayItHeads; 2uvoT9Z also moved the clamp and removed a duplicate zoom limit, and the p2p still pass.
OTHER GETTERS: Mine.draw also calls gameWorld.getTrack().getMaterialAt() for a mine lying in water, which still returns null from the GameWorld mock. A rocket has no such state, so no plausible rocket fix needs it.
FAILURE CHECK: every failing f2p in the 6 failing trials fails with the nop assertion values (278.8665°, 278.87335°, -0.34987 along the axis), so each is a real miss, not a harness rejection.
RESULT: every correct alternative seen in these trials, in Attempt4's trials and in the local variants passes.

dimensions.name: Hardening – Real & Feasible
dimensions.evidence: Defect 1 is upstream issue #362 (PR #373): the carried rocket is drawn over foreground map elements. Bugs 01-05 are plausible developer mistakes: a degrees/radians mix-up hidden behind normalizeAnglePiRad, a joint reference angle that keeps the wrong offset, a sprite axis swap for the exhaust, a radians-for-degrees mix-up in BodyRegionDrawer, a sign flip in the car shadow offset, and a +Y look-ahead rotated by (90 - heading). Each fix is a one- or two-line correction a real developer would write. The z-order fix is the upstream restructure, and simpler valid fixes also pass. Feasible: 2uvoT9Z solved all six from the video and the code in about 2 minutes of agent time, as afXQArC did in Attempt4.
